p8.riktningar-i-residual-stream.2: A common and well-supported hypothesis is that the model represents concepts as directions in the residual stream: “this is code”, “this is a negation”, “now I’m repeating myself”.
p8.riktningar-i-residual-stream.3: You find such a direction by running two groups of examples, with and without the property, and taking the difference between the mean activations in a layer:
p8.riktningar-i-residual-stream.4: r = mean(x | with) − mean(x | without) [4096] r̂ = r / ‖r‖ measure: x · r̂ scalar per token
p8.riktningar-i-residual-stream.5: A linear probe is the same idea trained as a classifier: if a linear boundary separates the groups, the information is there linearly in the stream.
p8.riktningar-i-residual-stream.6: 2D projection of a 4096-dimensional space. The points are made up.
p8.steering-och-ablation.2: Once the direction is found, you can intervene in the stream at runtime, with a hook in selected layers:
p8.steering-och-ablation.3: steering: x ← x + α · r̂ ablation: x ← x − (x · r̂) r̂
p8.steering-och-ablation.4: Steering pushes the model toward or away from the concept.
p8.steering-och-ablation.5: Ablation removes the component along r̂ entirely. Everything else in the vector is left untouched, but later layers can no longer read that signal.
p8.steering-och-ablation.6: Drag the sliders and see what happens to x and its projection onto r̂.
p8.baka-in-ablation-i-vikterna.2: Ablation via a hook needs extra code at inference time. But the same effect can be baked into the weights. Every matrix that writes to the stream, namely o_proj and down in each layer (and the embedding), can be projected so that it can never write along r̂:
p8.baka-in-ablation-i-vikterna.4: With our convention [d_in, d_out], the projection is multiplied in from the right, on the output side. No shape changes, so the modified model runs in vLLM like any other model.
p8.baka-in-ablation-i-vikterna.5: A typical approach looks like this: compare activations on responses that loop against responses that don’t, find a direction that grows before the repetition starts, and suppress it in the layers where it is strongest.
p8.baka-in-ablation-i-vikterna.6: The method is established, known from work on removing a model’s “refusal direction”. No new architecture is needed — only a projection into weights that already exist.
p8.baka-in-ablation-i-vikterna.7: You can now read a description like that and see exactly which tensors are touched: one vector r̂ [4096], a few [·, 4096] matrices per layer, and nothing else.
p8.vidare-harifran.3: vllm/model_executor/models/llama.py: the whole model with fused qkv and gate_up. Compare with the code in module 3.
p8.vidare-harifran.4: vllm/v1/engine/core.py: EngineCore and its step(). async_llm.py in the same directory is the frontend side.
p8.vidare-harifran.5: The scheduler and KV cache manager under vllm/v1/core/.
p8.vidare-harifran.6: Attention backends under vllm/v1/attention/: that is where block tables and slot mapping show up.
p8.vidare-harifran.7: The paths are for vLLM’s V1 engine and may move between versions.
p8.vidare-harifran.9: Start a small model, for example Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, and read the startup log: KV cache size in tokens and maximum concurrency.
p8.vidare-harifran.10: Measure TTFT and ITL with different --max-num-seqs and watch the curve from module 6.
p8.vidare-harifran.11: Send the same long system prompt twice and compare TTFT with and without prefix caching.
p8.vidare-harifran.13: Write a forward pass for a small Llama in plain PyTorch and check every shape against the trace in module 3.
p8.vidare-harifran.14: Add a KV cache and compare the speed with and without.
p8.vidare-harifran.15: Pull out the residual stream with a hook, compute a difference direction between two groups of prompts, and try ablation.
p8.vidare-harifran.17: Tokens become vectors, the vectors are refined by 32 layers that add to a shared stream, the last vector becomes a distribution over the next token, and an inference engine is almost entirely about keeping the KV cache in memory and reading the weights as few times as possible.
